typescript.command: npm run typecheck (server: tsc --noEmit, client: tsc -b --force)

eslint.command: npm run lint (server: eslint src scripts, client: eslint src)

prettier.note: every file matches the repo's Prettier config

unitAndIntegrationTests.framework: node:test + node:assert/strict, run against real generated artifacts (each *.service.test.ts drives the actual upstream pipeline rather than hand-shaped fixtures)

productionBuild.command: npm run build (server: tsc -p tsconfig.build.json, client: tsc -b && vite build)

duplicatedLogic.detail: 12 independent slugify implementations consolidated into 2 shared utilities (server/src/shared/utils/strings.ts, client/src/shared/lib/slugify.ts)

deadCode.method: ESLint no-unused-vars/no-unused-imports across every file (zero errors) plus a manual check that every module directory is registered in modules/index.ts (none orphaned)

circularDependencies.method: cross-module import grep audit (see architecture-summary.json) plus the strict types->lib->service->validator->controller->router layering that makes circularity structurally difficult to introduce

architectureViolations.method: grep audit for any module importing a sibling module's internals instead of shared/

largeFilesOrFunctions.detail: See architecture-summary.json's largeFileAudit — 11 are either data tables or code-generator template-literal files where line count doesn't track control-flow complexity; 1 (client shared/types/api.ts, 1471 lines) is a known, accepted tradeoff of the single-file type-mirror convention

generatedProjectQualityCapability.note: NexArch's Quality Engine (Phase 12) was exercised live against a real generated project (hotel booking platform, 82 backend + 94 frontend files) during this integration pass — the numbers below are that project's scores, demonstrating the platform's own quality-measurement capability, not NexArch's own codebase.

platformOwnEngineeringAssessment.note: A qualitative, evidence-based assessment of NexArch's own codebase (not generated-project output), scored on the same 9 categories its own Engineering Scorer uses, reasoned from the automated verification and code review above.

categoryScores.evidence: 15 modules, 0 cross-module import violations, 0 circular dependencies, consistent layering enforced everywhere

Helmet + strict-allow-list CORS + rate limiting + input validation on every endpoint + 0 hardcoded secrets found; docked slightly because the platform's own user-auth module is an intentional, documented Phase 3 scaffold (downstream generated apps get full JWT/RBAC via the Security Engine regardless)
Client production build in ~3.7s, 81KB gzipped main chunk with per-route code splitting, live API calls averaged 12.8ms across the full 27-call pipeline smoke test
0 TypeScript/ESLint errors, 227/227 tests passing, 1 real duplication found and fixed during this pass, consistent module conventions across all 12 build phases

227 automated tests, all server-side and all driven against real generated artifacts; the client itself has no automated frontend test suite yet, despite the platform being able to generate one — see recommendations
Comprehensive root README, per-module header documentation explaining every non-obvious decision, plus the platform generates full 10-document packages for every downstream project
NexArch ships its own docker-compose.yml/docker-compose.dev.yml/.github/workflows/ci.yml, and separately generates deployment infrastructure across 12 targets for downstream projects
One-command dev workflow (npm run dev), husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged, Cmd+K command palette, consistent design system, dark mode, 48 accessibility attributes across the console UI

recommendations: Add an automated frontend test suite (Vitest + Testing Library) for the NexArch client itself — the platform already generates this capability for downstream projects (Phase 12's frontend-test-generator.ts) but doesn't consume it on its own console.
Consider splitting client/src/shared/types/api.ts (1471 lines) into per-domain files once a 13th consumer makes the single-file convention genuinely unwieldy — not urgent today.
Build out the `auth` module (Phase 3 scope) if NexArch itself ever needs multi-user accounts beyond the current single-workspace, no-login console model.
